'''''Zuppa pavese''''' or '''''zuppa alla pavese''''' is an [[Italian cuisine|Italian]] [[soup]] consisting of [[broth]] into which slices of [[staling|stale bread]] and [[poached egg]]s are placed. It is generally served with grated [[Parmesan]].<ref>[[Elizabeth David]], ''Italian Food'', 1954, p. 53.</ref>

A legend claims that it was created by a peasant girl who added an egg to soup for King [[Francis I of France]] while he was being held prisoner after the [[Battle of Pavia]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Root |first=Waverley Lewis |title=The Food of Italy |last2=Chamberlain |first2=Samuel |date=1977 |publisher=Vintage Books |isbn=978-0-394-72429-4 |location=New York |pages=300}}</ref>

One way of preparing it is to place fried bread in a soup plate with cheese and a raw egg yolk on top. The hot broth is then poured over it, cooking the egg lightly.<ref name=":0" />
